[LTIM.1.1.3] `tz_offset_ns` is nanoseconds east of UTC, resolved by the
`local` member ([LTIM.3.2.1]); a `Time` the engine builds or reads from a slot
has offset 0 ([LTIM.14.1]). Once resolved, it is fixed for the lifetime of the value **within an
expression**. The value model carries it as an `Int64`
nanosecond quantity (a seconds-or-finer offset in ns exceeds `Int32`).
Local-time computation (`utc_ns + tz_offset_ns`) is a same-unit add —
no seconds-to-nanoseconds conversion in the arithmetic.

A `Time` stored in a **fact slot** persists the `utc_ns` instant only; the
resolved offset is an **expression-time** property and is **not** persisted
in working memory. A `Time` written to a slot and read back therefore comes
back UTC (`tz_offset_ns = 0`); re-zone it with `local` at use.
